definition.name: Soldier
definition.description:
Ability Scores: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution
Feat: Savage Attacker
Skill Proficiencies: Athletics and Intimidation
Tool Proficiency: Choose one kind of Gaming Set
Equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Spear, Shortbow, 20 Arrows, Gaming Set (same as above), Healer's Kit, Quiver, Traveler's Clothes, 14 GP; or (B) 50 GP

You began training for war as soon as you reached adulthood and carry precious few memories of life before you took up arms. Battle is in your blood. Sometimes you catch yourself reflexively performing the basic fighting exercises you learned first. Eventually, you put that training to use on the battlefield, protecting the realm by waging war.

race.description:
Found throughout the multiverse, humans are as varied as they are numerous.

Human Traits
Resourceful, Skillful, Versatile
race.longDescription:
Found throughout the multiverse, humans are as varied as they are numerous, and they endeavor to achieve as much as they can in the years they are given. Their ambition and resourcefulness are commended, respected, and feared on many worlds.

Humans are as diverse in appearance as the people of Earth, and they have many gods. Scholars dispute the origin of humanity, but one of the earliest known human gatherings is said to have occurred in Sigil, the torus-shaped city at the center of the multiverse and the place where the Common language was born. From there, humans could have spread to every part of the multiverse, bringing the City of Doors’ cosmopolitanism with them.

Human Traits

Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4–7 feet tall) or Small (about 2–4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet

definition.description: When determining your character’s ability scores, increase one score by 2 and a different one by 1, or increase three scores by 1. None of these increases can raise a score above 20.

definition.name: Languages
definition.description:
Your character knows at least three languages: Common plus two languages you roll or choose from the Standard Languages table. Knowledge of a language means your character can communicate in it, read it, and write it. Your class and other features might also give you languages.

The Standard Languages table lists languages that are widespread on D&D worlds. Every player character knows Common, which originated in the planar metropolis of Sigil, the hub of the multiverse. The other standard languages originated with the first members of the most prominent species in the worlds of D&D and have since spread widely.

Standard Languages
1d12 Language Origin
— Common Sigil
1 Common Sign Language Sigil
2 Draconic Dragons
3-4 Dwarvish Dwarves
5-6 Elvish Elves
7 Giant Giants
8 Gnomish Gnomes
9 Goblin Goblinoids
10-11 Halfling Halflings
12 Orc Orcs

definition.name: Greatsword
definition.description:
Proficiency with a Greatsword allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it.

This weapon has the following mastery property. To use this property, you must have a feature that lets you use it.

Graze. If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

definition.name: Backpack
definition.description: A Backpack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot. It can also serve as a saddlebag.

definition.name: Chain Mail, +1
definition.description: You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor.

definition.name: Plate
definition.description: Plate consists of shaped, interlocking metal plates to cover the entire body. A suit of plate includes gauntlets, heavy leather boots, a visored helmet, and thick layers of padding underneath the armor. Buckles and straps distribute the weight over the body.

definition.name: Rope, Hempen (50 feet)
definition.description: Rope, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

definition.name: Oil
definition.description:
You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel, as detailed below.

Dousing a Creature or an Object. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing an Oil flask. Target one creature or object within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or be covered in oil. If the target takes Fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an extra 5 Fire damage from burning oil.

Dousing a Space. You can take the Utilize action to pour an Oil flask on level ground to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. If lit, the oil burns until the end of the turn 2 rounds from when the oil was lit (or 12 seconds) and deals 5 Fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

Fuel. Oil serves as fuel for Lamps and Lanterns. Once lit, a flask of Oil burns for 6 hours in a Lamp or Lantern. That duration doesn’t need to be consecutive; you can extinguish the burning Oil (as a Utilize action) and rekindle it again until it has burned for a total of 6 hours.

definition.name: Tinderbox
definition.description: A Tinderbox is a small container holding flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a Candle, Lamp, Lantern, or Torch—or anything else with exposed fuel—takes a Bonus Action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

definition.name: Torch
definition.description: A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. When you take the Attack action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.

definition.name: Waterskin
definition.description: A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints. If you don’t drink sufficient water, you risk dehydration.

definition.name: Caltrops
definition.description: As a Utilize action, you can spread Caltrops from their bag to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 1 Piercing damage and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Caltrops.

definition.name: Alchemist's Fire
definition.description: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Alchemist’s Fire. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 1d4 Fire damage and start burning.

definition.name: Crowbar
definition.description: Using a Crowbar gives you Advantage on Strength checks where the Crowbar’s leverage can be applied.

definition.name: Fighter
definition.description:
A Master of All Arms and Armor

Fighters all share an unparalleled prowess with weapons and armor, and are well acquainted with death, both meting it out and defying it.

Primary Ability: Strength or Dexterity
Hit Point Die: D10
Saves: Strength & Constitution
definition.equipmentDescription:
Choose A, B, or C:
(A) Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, 8 Javelins, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 4 GP;
(B) Studded Leather Armor, Scimitar, Shortsword, Longbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 11 GP; or
(C) 155 GP

classFeatures.name: Core Fighter Traits
classFeatures.description:
As a Level 1 Character:

  • Gain all the traits in the Core Fighter Traits table.
  • Gain the Fighter’s level 1 features.
Core Fighter Traits
Primary Ability Strength or Dexterity
Hit Point Die D10 per Fighter level
Saving Throw Proficiencies Strength and Constitution
Skill Proficiencies Choose 2: Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Persuasion, Perception, or Survival
Weapon Proficiencies Simple and Martial weapons
Armor Training Light, Medium, and Heavy armor and Shields
Starting Equipment Choose A, B, or C: (A) Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, 8 Javelins, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 4 GP; (B) Studded Leather Armor, Scimitar, Shortsword, Longbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 11 GP; or (C) 155 GP

classFeatures.name: Fighting Style
classFeatures.description:
You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice.

Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.
classFeatures.summary: Specialize in a certain style of combat.

classFeatures.name: Second Wind
classFeatures.description:
You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.
classFeatures.summary: Draw on a limited well of physical and mental stamina to recover quickly.

classFeatures.name: Weapon Mastery
classFeatures.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.
classFeatures.summary: Unlock the mastery properties of your chosen weapons.

classFeatures.name: Action Surge
classFeatures.description:
You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

classFeatures.name: Tactical Mind
classFeatures.description: You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn’t expended.

classFeatures.name: Fighter Subclass
classFeatures.description: You gain a Fighter subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Fighter levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass’s features that are of your Fighter level or lower.

classFeatures.name: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 6, 8, 12, 14, and 16.

classFeatures.name: Extra Attack
classFeatures.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

classFeatures.name: Tactical Shift
classFeatures.description: Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a Bonus Action, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

classFeatures.name: 6: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 8, 12, 14, and 16.

classFeatures.name: 8: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 12, 14, and 16.

classFeatures.name: Indomitable
classFeatures.description:
If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can’t use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

You can use this feature twice before a Long Rest starting at level 13 and three times before a Long Rest starting at level 17.

classFeatures.name: Tactical Master
classFeatures.description: When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Push, Sap, or Slow property for that attack.

classFeatures.name: Two Extra Attacks
classFeatures.description: You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

classFeatures.name: 12: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 14 and 16.

classFeatures.name: Studied Attacks
classFeatures.description: You study your opponents and learn from each attack you make. If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

classFeatures.name: 14: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter level 16.

classFeatures.name: 16: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeatures.name: Epic Boon
classFeatures.description: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeatures.name: Three Extra Attacks
classFeatures.description: You can attack four times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

classFeatures.name: 4: Weapon Mastery
classFeatures.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of another Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of your weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.

classFeatures.name: 10: Weapon Mastery
classFeatures.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of another Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of your weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.

definition.iconicGear:

  • Every type of armor and shield

subclassDefinition.name: Champion
subclassDefinition.description:
Pursue Physical Excellence in Combat

A Champion focuses on the development of martial prowess in a relentless pursuit of victory.

classFeatures.name: Improved Critical
classFeatures.description: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

classFeatures.name: Remarkable Athlete
classFeatures.description:
Thanks to your athleticism, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Strength (Athletics) checks.

In addition, immediately after you score a Critical Hit, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

classFeatures.name: Additional Fighting Style
classFeatures.description: You gain another Fighting Style feat of your choice.

classFeatures.name: Heroic Warrior
classFeatures.description: The thrill of battle drives you toward victory. During combat, you can give yourself Heroic Inspiration whenever you start your turn without it.

classFeatures.name: Superior Critical
classFeatures.description: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can now score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18–20 on the d20.

classFeatures.name: Survivor
classFeatures.description:
You attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle, giving you these benefits.

Defy Death. You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws. Moreover, when you roll 18–20 on a Death Saving Throw, you gain the benefit of rolling a 20 on it.

Heroic Rally. At the start of each of your turns, you regain Hit Points equal to 5 plus your Constitution modifier if you are Bloodied and have at least 1 Hit Point.

definition.name: Heroic Warrior
definition.description: The thrill of battle drives you toward victory. During combat, you can give yourself Heroic Inspiration whenever you start your turn without it.
definition.snippet: During combat, you can give yourself Heroic Inspiration whenever you start your turn without it.

definition.name: Superior Critical
definition.description: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can now score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18–20 on the d20.

definition.name: Survivor
definition.description:
You attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle, giving you these benefits.

Defy Death. You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws. Moreover, when you roll 18–20 on a Death Saving Throw, you gain the benefit of rolling a 20 on it.

Heroic Rally. At the start of each of your turns, you regain Hit Points equal to 5 plus your Constitution modifier if you are Bloodied and have at least 1 Hit Point.
definition.snippet:
You gain the following benefits:
    • You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, and whenever you roll 18–20 on a Death Saving Throw, you gain the benefit of rolling a 20 on it.
    • At the start of each of your turns, If you have less than {{(maxhp/2)@rounddown}} HP and at least 1 Hit Point, you regain {{(5+modifier:con)#unsigned}} HP.

definition.name: Core Fighter Traits
definition.description:
As a Level 1 Character:

  • Gain all the traits in the Core Fighter Traits table.
  • Gain the Fighter’s level 1 features.
Core Fighter Traits
Primary Ability Strength or Dexterity
Hit Point Die D10 per Fighter level
Saving Throw Proficiencies Strength and Constitution
Skill Proficiencies Choose 2: Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Persuasion, Perception, or Survival
Weapon Proficiencies Simple and Martial weapons
Armor Training Light, Medium, and Heavy armor and Shields
Starting Equipment Choose A, B, or C: (A) Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, 8 Javelins, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 4 GP; (B) Studded Leather Armor, Scimitar, Shortsword, Longbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 11 GP; or (C) 155 GP
definition.multiClassDescription:
As a Multiclass Character:

  • Gain the following traits from the Core Fighter Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Martial weapons, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields.
  • Gain the Fighter’s level 1 features.
Core Fighter Traits
Primary Ability Strength or Dexterity
Hit Point Die D10 per Fighter level
Weapon Proficiencies Martial weapons
Armor Training Light and Medium armor and Shields

definition.name: Fighting Style
definition.description:
You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice.

Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.
definition.snippet: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice, and whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

definition.name: Second Wind
definition.description:
You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.
definition.snippet: As a Bonus Action, you can draw upon a limited well of physical and mental stamina and regain 1d10{{classlevel#signed}} HP. You can use this {{scalevalue}} times per Long Rest, and can regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest.

definition.name: Weapon Mastery
definition.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.

definition.name: Action Surge
definition.description:
You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.
definition.snippet:
On your turn you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

You can use this feature {{scalevalue}} time(s) until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

definition.name: Tactical Mind
definition.description: You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn’t expended.
definition.snippet: When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of Second Wind, and instead of regaining HP, you roll 1d10 and add the result to the ability check. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn’t expended.

definition.name: Fighter Subclass
definition.description: You gain a Fighter subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Fighter levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass’s features that are of your Fighter level or lower.

definition.name: Ability Score Improvement
definition.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 6, 8, 12, 14, and 16.

definition.name: Extra Attack
definition.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
definition.snippet: You can attack {{scalevalue}} times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

definition.name: Tactical Shift
definition.description: Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a Bonus Action, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
definition.snippet: Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a Bonus Action, you can move up to {{(speed/2)@rounddown}} ft. without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

definition.name: 6: Ability Score Improvement
definition.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 8, 12, 14, and 16.

definition.name: 8: Ability Score Improvement
definition.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 12, 14, and 16.

definition.name: Indomitable
definition.description:
If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can’t use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

You can use this feature twice before a Long Rest starting at level 13 and three times before a Long Rest starting at level 17.
definition.snippet:
If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a {{classlevel#signed}} bonus. You must use the new roll.

You can use this feature {{scalevalue}} time(s) per Long Rest.

definition.name: Tactical Master
definition.description: When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Push, Sap, or Slow property for that attack.
definition.snippet: When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Push, Sap, or Slow property for that attack.

definition.name: Two Extra Attacks
definition.description: You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

definition.name: 12: Ability Score Improvement
definition.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 14 and 16.

definition.name: Studied Attacks
definition.description: You study your opponents and learn from each attack you make. If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
definition.snippet: If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your turn.

definition.name: 14: Ability Score Improvement
definition.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter level 16.

definition.name: 16: Ability Score Improvement
definition.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

definition.name: Epic Boon
definition.description: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

definition.name: Three Extra Attacks
definition.description: You can attack four times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

definition.description:
General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+)

Increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. This feat can’t increase an ability score above 20.

Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once.

definition.name: Great Weapon Fighting
definition.description:
Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

When you roll damage for an attack you make with a Melee weapon that you are holding with two hands, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3. The weapon must have the Two-Handed or Versatile property to gain this benefit.
definition.snippet: When you roll damage for an attack you make with a Melee weapon that you are holding with two hands, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3. The weapon must have the Two-Handed or Versatile property.

definition.name: Savage Attacker
definition.description:
Origin Feat

You’ve trained to deal particularly damaging strikes. Once per turn when you hit a target with a weapon, you can roll the weapon’s damage dice twice and use either roll against the target.
definition.snippet: Once per turn when you hit a target with a weapon, you can roll the weapon’s damage dice twice and use either roll against the target.

definition.name: Skilled
definition.description:
Origin Feat

You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.

Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once.
definition.snippet: You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once.

definition.name: Soldier Ability Score Improvements
definition.description: The Soldier Background allows you to choose between Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution. Increase one of these scores by 2 and another one by 1, or increase all three by 1. None of these increases can raise a score above 20.

characterValues.value: Blade of the Disciple of the Five Headed’s Destroyer

2d8 Damage - Five Headed Destroyer’s Blessing: When the wielder rolls a natural 1 on any roll, the blade gains a luck charge (up to 3 per long rest). These charges can be used to add advantage to any attack, damage, or saving throw when Hagar is using the blade.  	- Parry: Up to three times per battle, When you are hit with a melee attack (after hit but before damage), you may use your reaction to add +2 to your AC for the purposes of that attack, possibly causing it to miss. Your AC returns to normal after you parry the attack.

definition.name: Warhammer (Push)
definition.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Warhammers:

Push. If you hit a creature with Warhammer, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.
definition.snippet: Push. If you hit a creature with Warhammer, you can push the creature up to 10 ft. straight away from you if it’s Large or smaller.

definition.name: Greatsword (Graze)
definition.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Greatswords:

Graze. If your attack roll with a Greatsword misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the Greatsword, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.
definition.snippet: Graze. If your attack roll with a Greatsword misses a creature, you can deal damage to it equal to the ability modifier used to make the attack. This damage is the same type dealt by the Greatsword, and can only be increased by increasing the ability modifier.

definition.name: Halberd (Cleave)
definition.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Halberds:

Cleave. If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a Halberd, you can make a melee attack roll with the Halberd against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the Halberd’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
definition.snippet: Cleave. Once per turn, if you hit a creature with a melee attack using a Halberd, you can make another melee attack with it against a second creature within 5 ft. of the first that’s within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the Halberd’s damage, but without your ability modifier (unless the modifier is negative).

Graze. If your attack roll with a Cleaver misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the Cleaver, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

options.label: Cannon (Push)
options.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Cannons:

Push. If you hit a creature with Cannon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

options.label: Atgeir (Pull)
options.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Atgeir:

Pull. If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can pull the creature 5 feet toward yourself if it is Large or smaller. When you do so, you can also move back 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and this does not use any of your normal movement speed.

options.label: Warhammer (Push)
options.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Warhammers:

Push. If you hit a creature with Warhammer, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

options.label: Halberd (Cleave)
options.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Halberds:

Cleave. If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a Halberd, you can make a melee attack roll with the Halberd against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the Halberd’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

options.label: Greatsword (Graze)
options.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Greatswords:

Graze. If your attack roll with a Greatsword misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the Greatsword, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

options.label: Mace (Sap)
options.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Maces:

Sap. If you hit a creature with a Mace, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

class.name: Second Wind
class.description:
You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.
class.snippet: You can draw upon a limited well of physical and mental stamina and regain 1d10{{classlevel#signed}} HP. You can use this {{limiteduse}} times per Long Rest, and can regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest.

class.name: Action Surge
class.description:
You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the [action]Magic[/action] action.

Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.
class.snippet:
On your turn you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

You can use this feature {{limiteduse}} time(s) until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

class.name: Tactical Mind
class.description: You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn’t expended.
class.snippet: When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of Second Wind, and instead of regaining HP, you roll 1d10 and add the result to the ability check. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn’t expended.

class.name: Improved Critical
class.description: Your attack rolls with weapons and [rules]unarmed strike;Unarmed Strikes[/rules] can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
class.snippet: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a Critical Hit on a d20 roll of 19 or 20.
